title: From showjumping to ghost hunting - meet the new boss of this Yorkshire museum
excerpt: Kirk Young, former showjumper and paranormal enthusiast, is appointed general manager of Eden Camp museum near Malton as it prepares for its 40th anniversary.
content:
From growing up on a farm and competing in showjumping to exploring the paranormal, Kirk Young has followed an unusual path to his new dream job in Yorkshire.

The journey has led him to Eden Camp Modern History Museum near Malton, where he has been appointed general manager.

Mr Young, who was raised on a farm and once represented Lancashire in showjumping, said: "When they offered me the position, I was absolutely ecstatic.

"I had planned to take some time out but, when this job was advertised, it was something I couldn't refuse.

"I've come to a place of work where the history I love and all my hobbies come together.

"It's a dream come true."

Eden Camp, a former prisoner-of-war camp, has operated as a museum since 1987 and attracts around 125,000 visitors each year.

It uses immersive storytelling, recreated scenes, and sensory experiences to bring wartime Britain to life, connecting generations with the realities of the past.

Mr Young brings a varied background to the role, with experience in hospitality, security, and logistics.

He also has a long-standing passion for military history, particularly the First and Second World Wars.

For the past 14 years, he has been a member of a paranormal club, through which he has explored military heritage sites and museums across Europe.

Mr Young said: "I thought I knew my stuff before I came here but no I don't.

"The team we have eat and breathe living history and the stories we tell.

"I've learned so much talking to the team and I can't wait to learn more and lead the site into what will be a really exciting chapter – with the 40th anniversary of Eden Camp coming up in 2027."

His appointment comes as Eden Camp begins a new era under the ownership of York-based Continuum Attractions, which acquired the site earlier this year.

Andrew Pawson, Continuum Attractions' CEO, said: "We're delighted to welcome Kirk to Eden Camp.

"His enthusiasm for history, passion for the guest experience and breadth of management experience make him a fantastic addition to the team.

"As we look ahead to the attraction's 40th anniversary in 2027, we're excited to have him at the helm, building on Eden Camp's remarkable legacy and helping shape an exciting future for a much-loved Yorkshire attraction."

The company has pledged to preserve the museum's heritage while investing in its future as one of Yorkshire's leading visitor attractions.

Plans for the future include continuing its development, with Mr Young tasked with guiding the attraction through its next phase of growth.

With the museum's milestone anniversary on the horizon, he said he is looking forward to working with the team to ensure Eden Camp continues to inspire, educate, and entertain visitors for years to come.

More information about the museum is available at edencamp.co.uk.
